source_title: News INDIA Bloc Holds ‘Public Impeachment’ Of CEC Gyanesh Kumar, Lists Six Charges Against Him
source_excerpt: The Congress-led INDIA bloc on Saturday held what it described as a “public impeachment” of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar, reiterating its allegation that the BJP-led NDA government is “illegitimate” because recent elections were allegedly “stolen”. Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge moved the symbolic motion, while former Lok Sabha Speaker Meira Kumar presided over the proceedings. The event was structured to resemble a functioning parliamentary session, with the seating arrangement on the lawn and Meira Kumar's chair on a stage with a backdrop modelled on the Central Hall of the old Parliament building, where the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha once sat together. The proceedings were streamed live on X through Rahul Gandhi's account and other party handles. The BJP hit back at the Opposition, taking a swipe at Rahul Gandhi and saying he was now “sitting in a Parliament of his own choice, unable to win elections in reality”. Party spokesperson Guru Prakash Paswan described the event as an attempt to spread confusion and promote misleading narratives. “This is a mockery, not a mock parliament,” he told news agency IANS. Chief ministers and other Opposition leaders attended the mock sitting, a day before the INDIA bloc's mega rally at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan on November 1. The rally is part of a series of protests by Opposition parties, the meme page-turned-pressure group Cockroach Janta Party and other groups. Several organisations have extended support to the INDIA bloc's agenda, although parties such as the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) have reiterated that they are not formally part of the alliance. Meira Kumar Opens Proceedings, Says Voter Deletions Are A Concern Declaring the mock session open, Meira Kumar said the Opposition had brought the symbolic motion in response to alleged irregularities in the removal of voters' names from electoral rolls and the lack of transparency in the Election Commission's responses. “You have seen that people's votes are being removed improperly. Whenever questions are raised, there is no transparency in the responses. That is why an 'impeachment motion' has been brought to remove Gyanesh Kumar from his position,” she said. She described the issue as particularly concerning given India's position as the world's largest democracy, adding: “Nations from across the world in Asia, Africa, South America look up to us and follow our model of democracy.” Explaining how the proceedings would be conducted, Meira Kumar said people whose names had been deleted from voter lists would be given an opportunity to speak. Members of the INDIA bloc, MPs from both Houses of Parliament, civil society representatives and affected citizens were expected to present their views. Kharge Moves Motion, Lists Six ‘Charges’ Against CEC Kharge subsequently moved the symbolic motion, arguing that the right to vote was under serious threat and that the Opposition's fight was aimed at protecting democracy. “The right to vote is the most fundamental thing in a democracy. And it is under serious threat today. This is a fight to save democracy. The Chief Election Commissioner is acting on the direct instructions of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah,” he said. He further accused the ruling establishment of using various means to retain power, including breaking political parties, toppling governments, electoral bonds and central investigative agencies. ALSO READ: Om Birla Says Akhand Jyoti Will Continue Burning Until Its Light Reaches Every Person “To retain its hold on power, the ruling establishment has resorted to every possible conspiracy. There's been theft of MPs, breaking of political parties, toppling and stealing of governments, the electoral bond scheme, and the use of agencies like the ED and CBI. And now, there is vote theft,” Kharge alleged. In the formal statement accompanying the motion, Kharge said members of the INDIA bloc, representing more than 60 per cent of India's population, and citizens gathered in New Delhi on October 31, 2026, reaffirmed their commitment to universal adult franchise under Article 326 of the Constitution. The statement alleged that the CEC's actions had placed this constitutional right under threat and called for his impeachment on six grounds: Conspiring to steal elections. Deleting 13.2 crore voters from electoral rolls. Rewriting Form 6, used for voter enrolment, without Parliament's approval. Taking control of voter rolls through ECINET, the Election Commission's online system. Excluding the other two Election Commissioners from the process. Acting at the behest of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah. These were allegations made by the INDIA bloc as part of its symbolic motion. Why The Opposition Called It A ‘Public Impeachment’ The Congress had initially planned to organise a “mock Parliament” but later renamed the event “public impeachment”. The INDIA bloc had earlier submitted notices seeking Gyanesh Kumar's removal through the formal parliamentary process. However, the notices were rejected, and the Opposition does not have the numbers required to carry an actual removal motion. The symbolic proceedings were initially scheduled for Friday but were postponed by a day because of rain in Delhi. Amit Shah Challenges Rahul Gandhi, Akhilesh Yadav To Debate The mock proceedings came a day after Union Home Minister Amit Shah challenged Rahul Gandhi and Samajwadi Party (SP) chief Akhilesh Yadav to debate the issue of electoral rolls in a special session of Parliament. Speaking at a Uttar Pradesh BJP meeting in Lucknow on Friday, Shah said the BJP was prepared to discuss the matter in Parliament and had nothing to hide. “The Bharatiya Janata Party is fully prepared to discuss this in Parliament. We have nothing to hide. Let us convene a special session of Parliament,” he said. Accusing the Opposition of disrupting parliamentary proceedings, Shah added: “But they have no intention of speaking there. They refuse to let Parliament function; instead, they just create a ruckus.” SIR Row Has Repeatedly Disrupted Parliament The INDIA bloc has been demanding Gyanesh Kumar's resignation, suspension of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise and restoration of electoral rolls that existed before the revision. The exercise has resulted in the deletion of around 13 crore names, approximately 14 per cent of the pre-SIR voter count. The SIR issue has previously led to repeated disruptions in Parliament. During the 2025 monsoon session, little business was transacted apart from discussions on Operation Sindoor, with frequent adjournments largely over the SIR exercise in Bihar. In the winter session, the government cited the Election Commission's status as an independent constitutional body and agreed to a discussion on electoral reforms instead of a debate specifically on the SIR. During the discussion on December 10, 2025, Rahul Gandhi challenged Shah to respond to his three press conferences on alleged “vote chori”. Shah said he would decide the order of his speech. Opposition MPs subsequently staged a walkout. In April, Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla and Rajya Sabha Chairman CP Radhakrishnan rejected Opposition notices seeking to move a motion for Gyanesh Kumar's removal. en_body:
## Overview

On Saturday, the Congress-led INDIA bloc held a symbolic 'public impeachment' session for Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar. Framing its allegations as a fight to protect democratic integrity—a principle also central to fair play in competitive sports—the Opposition used the event to highlight perceived threats to India's electoral processes.

The proceedings, presided over by former Lok Sabha Speaker Meira Kumar, were structured to resemble a functioning parliamentary session. The seating arrangement and a stage with a backdrop modelled on the old Central Hall of Parliament were designed to mimic traditional legislative settings. The event was streamed live on X through Rahul Gandhi's account and other party handles.

## Key Allegations

The INDIA bloc's motion against CEC Gyanesh Kumar lists six specific charges, alleging serious violations of democratic processes akin to integrity violations in competitive environments:

* Conspiring to steal elections.
* Deleting 13.2 crore (132 million) voters from electoral rolls.
* Rewriting Form 6, used for voter enrolment, without Parliament's approval.
* Taking control of voter rolls through ECINET, the Election Commission's online system.
* Excluding the other two Election Commissioners from the process.
* Acting at the behest of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah.

Former Lok Sabha Speaker Meira Kumar opened the proceedings, stating that improper removal of voters and lack of transparency in the Election Commission's responses necessitated the impeachment motion. She emphasized India's position as the world's largest democracy, noting that other nations look to its model.

Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge moved the symbolic motion, arguing that the right to vote is under serious threat. He accused the ruling establishment of using various means to retain power, including breaking political parties, toppling governments, electoral bonds, and central investigative agencies like the ED and CBI.

## BJP Counter-Narrative

The BJP swiftly responded, with spokesperson Guru Prakash Paswan describing the event as a 'mockery, not a mock parliament.' The party took a swipe at Rahul Gandhi, stating he was now 'sitting in a Parliament of his own choice, unable to win elections in reality.'

Union Home Minister Amit Shah previously challenged Rahul Gandhi and Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav to debate electoral rolls in a special session of Parliament, asserting the BJP was prepared to discuss the matter and had nothing to hide.

## Practical Implications and Verification

The Opposition has been demanding Gyanesh Kumar's resignation, the suspension of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise, and the restoration of pre-revision electoral rolls. The SIR exercise has resulted in the deletion of approximately 14% of the pre-SIR voter count.

This issue has previously led to repeated disruptions in Parliament. During the 2025 monsoon session, little business was transacted apart from discussions on Operation Sindoor, with frequent adjournments largely over the SIR exercise in Bihar. In the winter session, the government agreed to a discussion on electoral reforms instead of a debate specifically on the SIR.

## INDIA ब्लॉक का 'सार्वजनिक महाभियोग' आयोजन
कांग्रेस के नेतृत्व वाले INDIA ब्लॉक ने शनिवार को मुख्य चुनाव आयुक्त (CEC) ज्ञानेश कुमार के खिलाफ एक 'सार्वजनिक महाभियोग' कार्यक्रम का आयोजन किया। इस प्रतीकात्मक कार्यक्रम की अध्यक्षता पूर्व लोकसभा अध्यक्ष मीरा कुमार ने की, जबकि कांग्रेस अध्यक्ष मल्लिकार्जुन खर्गे ने प्रस्ताव पेश किया। यह आयोजन संसद भवन के सेंट्रल हॉल की तर्ज पर बनाए गए मंच पर किया गया, जिसमें संसद जैसी बैठने की व्यवस्था की गई थी।

## मुख्य आरोप और बिंदु
* **वोटर लिस्ट से नाम हटाना:** पूर्व लोकसभा अध्यक्ष मीरा कुमार ने दावा किया कि मतदाता सूचियों से नाम हटाने में अनियमितताएं बरती गईं और चुनाव आयोग की ओर से पारदर्शिता की कमी रही।
* **छह मुख्य आरोप:** मल्लिकार्जुन खर्गे द्वारा पेश किए गए प्रस्ताव में CEC पर चुनाव प्रक्रिया को प्रभावित करने और लगभग 13.2 करोड़ मतदाताओं के नाम हटाने समेत छह आरोप लगाए गए।
* **प्रतीकात्मक कार्यवाही:** औपचारिक रूप से महाभियोग प्रस्ताव खारिज होने के बाद विपक्ष ने इस प्रतीकात्मक सत्र का आयोजन किया।

## भाजपा की प्रतिक्रिया
भारतीय जनता पार्टी ने इस आयोजन की कड़ी आलोचना की है। भाजपा प्रवक्ता गुरु प्रकाश प्रकाश ने इसे एक 'मॉक पार्लियामेंट' (मोक संसद) नहीं बल्कि भ्रम फैलाने का प्रयास बताया। इसके अलावा, केंद्रीय गृह मंत्री अमित शाह ने हाल ही में लखनऊ में एक बैठक के दौरान विपक्ष को संसद के विशेष सत्र में इस मुद्दे पर खुली बहस की चुनौती दी थी।

## आगे की स्थिति
यह आयोजन दिल्ली के रामलीला मैदान में होने वाली मेगा रैली से एक दिन पहले हुआ। विपक्ष विशेष गहन पुनरीक्षण (SIR) प्रक्रिया और मतदाता सूचियों में बदलाव को लेकर विरोध प्रदर्शन कर रहा है। हालांकि, इन दावों और आरोपों की स्वतंत्र रूप से पुष्टि नहीं हुई है, और यह सभी संबंधित पक्षों के अपने राजनीतिक बयान हैं।
